cards.en: In the UK, people often call dessert pudding.
cards.gram: pudding = 영국에서 '디저트'를 부르는 말. 꼭 푸딩이 아니어도 돼요.

cards.en: I have a really sweet tooth.
cards.gram: have a sweet tooth = 단 걸 좋아하다. I like sweet tooth ❌ → have를 써요.

cards.ko: 레몬은 너무 셔서 그냥은 못 먹어요.
cards.en: Lemons are too sour to eat on their own.
cards.gram: sour = 신맛이 나는. too 형용사 to 동사 = 너무 ~해서 ~할 수 없다.

cards.en: This yoghurt tastes quite sharp.

cards.ko: 케이크가 너무 배불러서 다 못 먹었어요.
cards.en: The cake was so filling that I couldn't finish it.
I'm a chocolate person.
cards.gram: a + 좋아하는 것 + person = ~을 정말 좋아하는 사람. a coffee person, a dog person.

cards.ko: 저는 애피타이저보다 디저트를 먹는 게 더 좋아요.
cards.en: I'd rather have a dessert than a starter.
cards.gram: I'd rather + 동사원형 + A + than B = B보다 A가 더 좋아요. starter = 영국식 '애피타이저'.

cards.ko: 저는 집에서 만든 디저트를 제일 좋아해요.
cards.en: I like homemade desserts the most.
cards.gram: homemade = 집에서 만든. homemade bread, homemade food.

cards.en: On a hot day, you can't beat ice cream.
I only have cake as a treat on special occasions.
cards.gram: as a treat = 특별히 나에게 주는 선물로. special occasion = 특별한 날.

cards.ko: 저는 밥 먹고 나면 단 게 엄청 당겨요.
cards.en: I get strong sugar cravings after meals.
cards.gram: sugar cravings = 단 게 당기는 것. get cravings 형태로 써요.

cards.ko: 그게 제가 먹어 본 디저트 중에 최고였어요.
cards.en: It was the best dessert I've ever had.
cards.gram: the best + 명사 + I've ever had = 지금까지 먹어 본 것 중 최고. Part 2 경험 묘사에 좋아요.

cards.ko: 저는 단 간식보다 짭짤한 간식이 더 좋아요.
cards.en: I prefer savoury snacks to sweet ones.
cards.gram: savoury = 짭짤한(단맛이 아닌). prefer A to B = B보다 A를 더 좋아하다.

cards.ko: 겉이 바삭한 애플 크럼블을 정말 좋아해요.
cards.en: I love apple crumble with a crispy topping.

cards.ko: 이 초콜릿 케이크는 저한테 너무 진해요.
cards.en: This chocolate cake is too rich for me.
cards.gram: rich (음식) = 진하고 기름진, 무거운 맛. 돈이 많다는 뜻만 있는 게 아니에요.

cards.ko: 튀긴 음식은 맛있지만 건강에 별로 좋지 않아요.
cards.en: Deep-fried food is tasty, but it isn't very healthy.
cards.gram: deep-fried = 기름에 푹 튀긴. isn't very + 형용사 = 별로 ~하지 않다.

cards.en: What do you mean by that?
cards.gram: What do you mean by ~? = ~가 무슨 뜻이에요? 상대 말을 잘 못 알아들었을 때 써요. 예: What do you mean by 'pudding'?

cards.ko: 제 가장 친한 친구가 저에게 신부 들러리를 부탁했어요.
cards.en: My best friend asked me to be her bridesmaid.
cards.gram: bridesmaid = 신부 들러리. maid of honour = 가장 중요한 들러리.

cards.ko: 저는 형 결혼식에서 신랑 들러리를 했어요.
cards.en: I was the best man at my brother's wedding.

cards.ko: 결혼 전에 친구들이랑 처녀 파티를 했어요.
cards.en: We had a hen party before her wedding.
cards.gram: hen party = 신부의 결혼 전 파티, stag party = 신랑의 결혼 전 파티.

cards.en: We had a traditional wedding.
I'd like a low-key wedding.
I've got a wedding coming up soon.
I haven't been to a wedding for ages.
cards.gram: for ages = 오랫동안. haven't been to ~ = ~에 안 가 봤다.

cards.en: It became a bit samey.
There are quite a few hidden costs at weddings.
cards.gram: hidden costs = 숨은 비용. quite a few = 꽤 많은.

cards.en: I just enjoy a party.
cards.gram: enjoy a party = 파티를 즐기다. 사교 행사 좋아한다고 말할 때.

cards.ko: 많은 사람 앞에서 축사를 해야 했어요.
cards.en: I had to make a speech in front of lots of people.
cards.gram: make a speech = 연설·축사를 하다. in front of = ~ 앞에서.

cards.ko: 새 옷을 사야 할 때도 있어요.
cards.en: Sometimes you have to buy a new outfit.
An octopus has eight tentacles.
Plastic is a big threat to the ocean.
Air pollution is bad in my city.
I try to use less single-use plastic.
I live near the seaside.

cards.ko: 제가 제일 좋아하는 바다 동물은 돌고래예요.
cards.en: My favourite sea creature is the dolphin.
Dolphins are really intelligent.
Hold on, I don't think I agree.
That plastic ends up in the ocean.
The oceans are not in good condition.
I saw a video of a turtle stuck in plastic.
That's a difficult question for me to answer.
cards.gram: a difficult question for me to answer = 대답하기 어려운 질문. Part 1에서 시간 벌 때.

cards.en: I always feel nervous before an interview.

cards.ko: 저는 제 영어 실력에 꽤 자신 있어요.
cards.en: I'm fairly confident about my English.
I have good communication skills.

cards.ko: 구체적인 예를 들어 설명하는 게 좋아요.
cards.en: It's good to give examples.
Job interviews are a little bit stressful.
It's natural to be nervous.

cards.ko: 걱정이 안 된다면 신경을 안 쓴다는 뜻이에요.
cards.en: If you're not worried, it means you don't care.
I really want it to go well.
cards.gram: go well = 잘 되다. want it to ~.

cards.ko: 친절함과 자신감 사이 균형을 찾기 어려워요.
cards.en: It's hard to find a balance between being friendly and confident.
cards.gram: find a balance between A and B = A와 B 사이 균형을 찾다.

cards.en: You should prepare before the interview.
That's not a good sign.
I have some experience in this field.
cards.gram: experience = 경험(셀 수 없는 명사로 쓸 때 a 없이).

cards.en: Namsan Tower is a famous landmark in Seoul.

cards.ko: 저는 여행 가면 관광을 많이 해요.
cards.en: I do a lot of sightseeing when I travel.
I went on a guided tour of the palace.
It's funny you should ask, because I went last week.
cards.gram: It's funny you should ask = 마침 물어보시네요.

cards.en: It's a really famous place that everyone knows.
cards.gram: a place that everyone knows = 모두가 아는 곳.

cards.en: I like visiting historic buildings.
It's always crowded with tourists.
It's a must-see.
I saw a concert at a famous concert hall.
The guide told us about the history.
The view was amazing.
I took lots of photos.

cards.ko: 저는 영화 시작 전 예고편 보는 걸 좋아해요.
cards.en: I like watching the trailers before the film.
I always get popcorn at the cinema.

cards.ko: 그 영화의 액션 장면은 정말 장관이었어요.
cards.en: The action scenes were spectacular.
There are too many distractions at home.

cards.ko: 저는 영화관에서 보는 게 더 좋아요.
cards.en: I prefer watching films at the cinema.

cards.ko: 어젯밤에 집에서 정말 좋은 영화를 봤어요.
cards.en: I watched a really good film at home last night.
It's different on the big screen.
cards.gram: on the big screen = 영화관 큰 화면으로.

cards.ko: 영화 중에 휴대폰 보는 사람이 짜증 나요.
cards.en: People who check their phones during a film annoy me.
I watched it on my sofa with my housemates.
Cinema tickets are quite expensive these days.
I'm a big fan of action films.
cards.gram: I'm a big fan of ~ = ~를 정말 좋아해요.

cards.en: I stay until the end of the credits.
I checked in two hours before my flight.
I almost lost my boarding pass.

cards.ko: 보안 검색대 통과하는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
cards.en: It took ages to go through security.
I waited at the boarding gate.
I had to catch a 6 a.m. flight.
I once missed a flight because I was late.
I've got a trip coming up soon.
cards.gram: have a trip coming up = 곧 여행이 있다.

cards.en: I checked my bag.
I like getting to the airport early.
My flight was delayed by an hour.
I prefer a window seat.
cards.gram: window seat = 창가 좌석, aisle seat = 통로 좌석.

cards.en: I enjoy looking around the duty-free shops.

cards.ko: 비 오는 날 집에 있으면 아늑해요.
cards.en: It feels cosy to stay at home on rainy days.
In the UK, people light bonfires in autumn.
I watched the fireworks on New Year's Eve.

The weather's getting a little bit cooler.
The leaves are starting to fall from the trees.
It's not summer anymore.
Autumn is my favourite season.

I get out my thick jumpers in autumn.
The nights are getting longer.

cards.ko: 제 첫 직장은 정말 스트레스가 많았어요.
cards.en: My first job was really stressful.

cards.ko: 하루 종일 서 있는 건 정말 지쳐요.
cards.en: Standing all day is exhausting.
My noisy neighbour is really annoying.
Don't take it personally when customers get angry.
cards.gram: take it personally = 자기한테 하는 말로 받아들이다.

cards.ko: 그 말을 너무 마음에 담아 두지 마세요.
cards.en: Don't take it to heart.
cards.gram: take it to heart = 마음에 깊이 담아 두다.

cards.en: There's one job in particular that I remember.
That's intriguing!

cards.ko: 그 일 때문에 오히려 돈을 잃었어요.
cards.en: That job actually made me lose money.
I'm completely exhausted after work.
The pay was really low.
But I learnt a lot from it.
cards.gram: learn a lot from ~ = ~에서 많이 배우다. learnt(영국) = learned.

cards.ko: 다시는 그 일 안 할 거예요.
cards.en: I'd never do that job again.
I complained to the waiter because my food was cold.
I made a complaint to the hotel.
cards.gram: make a complaint = 정식으로 항의하다. complaint는 명사.

cards.en: I got a student discount.
I felt I was entitled to a refund.

cards.ko: 저는 식당 가기 전에 리뷰를 확인해요.
cards.en: I always check the reviews before I go to a restaurant.
If there's a problem, I tell someone straight away.

cards.ko: 저는 불평을 잘 안 하는 편이에요.
cards.en: I don't usually complain.
The room looked completely different from the photos.
They apologised politely.
The service wasn't good enough.
cards.gram: not good enough = 충분히 좋지 않은, 기대에 못 미치는.

cards.en: Bad reviews make me worried.
Next time, I'll go somewhere else.
I do most of my housework at the weekend.
My least favourite chore is washing the dishes.
cards.gram: chore = 집안일 하나하나. least favourite = 제일 싫어하는.

cards.ko: 저는 일주일에 두 번 빨래를 해요.
cards.en: I do the laundry twice a week.
I hoovered the living room.
I swept the kitchen floor.
Then I mop the floor.
I keep putting off the ironing.
I had a lot to do this weekend.
cards.gram: have a lot to do = 할 일이 많다.

cards.ko: 손님 오기 전에 집을 준비해야 했어요.
cards.en: We had to get the house ready.
I try to keep my home clean and tidy.
I'm a little bit tired, but I'm good.
I listen to music while I clean.
I take my coffee white.
cards.gram: take one's coffee white / black = 커피를 우유 넣어서 / 블랙으로 마시다.

cards.en: Coffee has a lot of caffeine.
I drink decaf in the evening.
I'm trying to cut down on coffee.
cards.gram: cut down on / cut back on ~ = ~을 줄이다.

cards.en: I prefer my coffee hot.
My coffee's got a bit cool.
I have two cups of coffee a day.
Coffee helps me stay alert.

cards.ko: 두 번째 커피를 다 마시면 슬퍼요.
cards.en: It's a sad moment when I've finished my second coffee.
cards.gram: It's a sad moment when ~ = ~할 때가 슬픈 순간이에요.

cards.ko: 저는 아이스커피를 일 년 내내 마셔요.
cards.en: I drink iced coffee all year round.
I can't wake up without coffee in the morning.
Oh, that's a shame.
